correctness.rationale: For J(n,2)=L(K_n), an edge set totally dominates if and only if its spanning graph has at most one isolated vertex and no isolated K2 component. If k selected edges form c nontrivial components with epsilon isolates and cycle rank s, then n-epsilon=k+c-s and c<=floor(k/2). At equality k=ceil(2(n-1)/3), all possible residue classes force s=0 and exactly the listed component-size combinations. Cayley counts for trees on 3,4,5 vertices are 3,16,125, and labeled set-partition factors yield each of the stated factorial expressions without overcounting. The standalone direct adjacency verifier exhausts every k-minimal-size subset for n=4..9 and agrees exactly.

originality.rationale: The close new Johnson-graph preprint determines the scalar total domination number, which is explicitly prior coverage. The accepted claim instead classifies every optimum and gives residue-class factorial formulas for the number of optimal vertex subsets. Searches included triangular-graph, line-graph-of-complete-graph and total-edge-domination aliases, together with extremal forest and exact enumeration formulations. value.rationale: The current Johnson-graph total-domination literature explicitly singles out gamma_t(J(n,2)) as an exact new scalar value. Counting all extremizers reveals a nontrivial three-residue transition, distinct tree-component structures, and exact labeled multiplicities with factorial growth. The result refines the extremal problem with exact solution-space size, useful for extremal-set sampling, uniqueness/orbit questions, and structural comparisons. The five-vertex-tree and paired-four-vertex-tree exceptions are motivated by the tight deficit in the existing optimum, not arbitrary extra graph slices.
